## Declarations and implementations

```plato

    //==
    // # Vector3D — cross-product neighbourhood (cross-product lesson)
    //
    // Cross(Vector3D, Vector3D) itself is an intrinsic (intrinsics.library.plato;
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross_product); these are the helpers that
    // sit immediately around it. Concrete Vector3D receivers so Cross and the
    // component accessors resolve to the 3D type.

    // The scalar triple product a . (b x c): the signed volume of the
    // parallelepiped spanned by the three vectors; zero iff they are coplanar
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scalar_triple_product).
    ScalarTriple(a: Vector3D, b: Vector3D, c: Vector3D): Number
        => a.Dot(b.Cross(c));

    // True when a and b point along the same line (parallel or antiparallel),
    // judged by the length of their cross product relative to tolerance. Zero
    // vectors are treated as parallel to everything. tolerance is an absolute
    // bound on the cross-product magnitude.
    AreParallel(a: Vector3D, b: Vector3D, tolerance: Number): Boolean
        => a.Cross(b).MagnitudeSquared <= tolerance * tolerance;

    // The wedge (exterior) product a ^ b as a Bivector3D — the geometric-algebra
    // dual of the cross product under the shared right-hand convention: the
    // bivector components (YZ, ZX, XY) equal the (X, Y, Z) of a x b. Encodes the
    // oriented plane element (area and orientation) spanned by a and b.
    Wedge(a: Vector3D, b: Vector3D): Bivector3D
        => (
            a.Y * b.Z - a.Z * b.Y,
            a.Z * b.X - a.X * b.Z,
            a.X * b.Y - a.Y * b.X);

    //==
    // # Vector2D — planar perp and signed area (2D cross-product analog)
    //
    // 2D has no cross product; the honest planar primitives are the perpendicular
    // and the scalar (z-component) cross. Naming them here keeps 2D code from
    // faking a 3D cross.

    // The left perpendicular of v: v rotated +90 degrees (CCW), (-Y, X). Same
    // length as v; the right perpendicular is its negation.
    Perp(v: Vector2D): Vector2D
        => (-v.Y, v.X);

    // The 2D scalar cross (perp-dot) a.X*b.Y - a.Y*b.X: the signed area of the
    // parallelogram spanned by a and b, positive when b is CCW from a. Equals the
    // z-component of the 3D cross of the lifted vectors.
    Cross(a: Vector2D, b: Vector2D): Number
        => a.X * b.Y - a.Y * b.X;

    //==
    // # Direction2D / Direction3D — validated factories (normalization pitfalls)
    //
    // Convention: see CONVENTIONS.md - Partial operations. `FromVector`
    // normalizes and carries a non-zero precondition; `TryFromVector` is the
    // total fallback form; `FromVectorUnchecked` wraps without normalizing and is
    // only correct when the argument is already unit length.

    // The unit direction of v. Precondition: v is non-zero (its length becomes the
    // divisor); zero input is undefined. Use TryFromVector for a total path.
    FromVector(v: Vector2D): Direction2D
        => Direction2D(v.Normalize);

    // The unit direction of v, or fallback when v has (near) zero length. Total.
    TryFromVector(v: Vector2D, fallback: Direction2D): Direction2D
        => v.MagnitudeSquared > 0.0 ? Direction2D(v.Normalize) : fallback;

    // Wraps v as a Direction2D WITHOUT normalizing. Unsafe: the caller asserts v
    // is already unit length; violating that silently breaks the Direction2D
    // invariant. Prefer FromVector unless the unit length is already established.
    FromVectorUnchecked(v: Vector2D): Direction2D
        => Direction2D(v);

    // The unit direction of v. Precondition: v is non-zero; zero input is
    // undefined. Use TryFromVector for a total path.
    FromVector(v: Vector3D): Direction3D
        => Direction3D(v.Normalize);

    // The unit direction of v, or fallback when v has (near) zero length. Total.
    TryFromVector(v: Vector3D, fallback: Direction3D): Direction3D
        => v.MagnitudeSquared > 0.0 ? Direction3D(v.Normalize) : fallback;

    // Wraps v as a Direction3D WITHOUT normalizing. Unsafe: the caller asserts v
    // is already unit length; violating that silently breaks the Direction3D
    // invariant. Prefer FromVector unless the unit length is already established.
    FromVectorUnchecked(v: Vector3D): Direction3D
        => Direction3D(v);

    //==
    // # VectorN

    // Folds component hashes in index order.
    Hash(self: VectorN): Integer
        => self.Components.Reduce(0, (acc, x) => acc * 31 + x.Hash);
}
```
